flags.assumption: The division `(bad + good) / 2` assumes `bad + good` will not be negative (or that truncation towards zero behaves identically to Python floor division), but when `bad = -1` and `good = 0` (which would require `good - bad > 1`, so not immediately entered, but e.g. `bad = -1, good = 1` yields sum `0`), wait: if `bad = -1` and `good = 2`, `mid = 1 / 2 = 0`. What if `good = 0`? The loop condition `good - bad > 1` means `good - bad >= 2`. If `good = 0`, `bad <= -2`. But `bad` starts at -1 and either stays -1 or becomes `mid >= 0`. So `bad` is always >= -1, and since `good - bad >= 2`, `good >= 1`. Therefore `bad + good >= 0` always!

site.reason: Negative indices count from the end in Python (xs[-1] is the last item); Java throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Python reads whole lines; Java Scanner reads whitespace-separated tokens, and nextLine() after nextInt() returns the rest of the current line, often an empty string.
Python int() accepts any size; Java Integer.parseInt and Scanner.nextInt throw for values outside int range, so the translation must choose int, long or BigInteger.
